messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: Bench-scale batch slurry sorption tests with clearly defined CAC dose, L/S ratio, equilibration time, and PFAS concentration range are documented in the cited passages, so judging the data as comparable with conditions to similar batch systems is a reasonable inference.
The cited results report PFAS removal percentages from solution, so classifying the endpoint as 'removal' is consistent with the source.
The cited text discusses solid–liquid distribution coefficients (Kd) and sorption behavior, which supports classifying this endpoint as 'sorption'.

The methods describe soil–CAC slurry batch tests using low-organic soil and Milli-Q water with CaCl2 rather than realistic groundwater or fixed beds; inferring scalability limitations from this design is justified.
The methods explicitly state that only seven PFAS were tested; inferring a limitation due to exclusion of many other PFAS is justified.
The matrix description matches the methods: low-organic soil (0.6% OC) mixed with colloidal activated carbon and Milli-Q water containing 1 mM CaCl2 at L/S = 20.
The value describes PlumeStop CAC with 20% AC, ~900 m²/g surface area, 1–2 µm particles, and zeta potential −80 to −2 mV at pH 7, all of which are present in the cited methods passage.
No single numeric unit is appropriate for this descriptive field; leaving the unit null is consistent with the qualitative nature of the value.
The CAC dose of 0.2% w/w (0.004 g CAC per 2 g soil) is explicitly stated in the cited text.
The dose is expressed as a mixed textual description including % w/w and g per g soil; leaving the unit null is acceptable for this compound description.
The liquid-to-solid ratio L/S = 20 is directly reported in the cited methods passage.
L/S is a dimensionless ratio; leaving the unit null is appropriate.
The background electrolyte concentration of 1 mM CaCl2 in Milli-Q water is clearly given in the cited text.
The unit mM matches the reported 1 mM CaCl2 concentration.
An equilibration time of 14 days is explicitly stated in the methods passage.
The unit 'days' correctly reflects the reported equilibration time.
The PFAS concentration range of 0.002–0.05 mmol/L is directly reported in the experimental description.
The unit mmol/L matches the reported concentration range.
All seven PFAS listed (PFPeA, PFHpA, PFNA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS, FOSA) are explicitly named in the cited methods passage as the compounds tested.
Average PFAS removal in single-solute systems is reported as 77%±7.8%; the extracted value 77 matches the source.
The source reports removal in percent; unit '%' is correct.
The standard deviation of average removal is 7.8% in the source; the extracted value 7.8 matches exactly.
The variability is expressed in percent; unit '%' is appropriate.
The maximum single-solute removal is reported as about 99.8% for FOSA at 0.002 mmol/L; the extracted value 99.8 matches this figure.
Removal is reported in percent; unit '%' is correct.
The minimum single-solute removal is reported as 41% for PFOS at 0.05 mmol/L; the extracted value 41 matches the source.
Removal is reported in percent; unit '%' is correct.

The cited passages only discuss sorption efficiencies and Kd values with no mention of transformation products or fluoride release; inferring that the process is adsorption without chemical degradation is consistent with the available text.
The methods describe bench-scale batch adsorption experiments using soil–CAC slurries, matching the extracted study-scale description.
The treatment description (PlumeStop, 20% AC, mixed with soil at 0.2% w/w) is explicitly stated in the CAC and soil properties methods passage.

result.record_usable_rationale: All core elements—source identity, matrix, treatment (colloidal activated carbon in soil–water slurry), PFAS scope, operating conditions, endpoints, and quantitative removal data—are directly supported by the cited passages with no material contradictions or transcription errors, so the record is suitable for quantitative synthesis.
